clue.text: Range for cooking crumpets

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters of the next word are being worked over and mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen stove that suits the making of crumpets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a cooker, fitting the crumpets, but it is the definition; 'cooking' rearranges CRUMPETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full span or scope of values, so it is a synonym for a range.

clue.text: Like some kings and queens having power advanced

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
advanced in the sense of ahead of time, before the expected hour

explanation.surface: Royalty who hold power and have come forward in time.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London street traders who wear costumes covered in mother-of-pearl buttons, a Cockney charity tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: The costermonger royalty of London are known by the pearl buttons sewn over their clothes, an idiom-like title.

clue.text: Attractiveness of cleaner maiden

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British term for a woman paid to clean houses
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady's young assistant has a certain appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is an old British word for a cleaning woman; M stands for a maiden over in cricket, one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is the power of pleasing or attracting people, a direct synonym for attractiveness.

clue.text: Scrap dud tanner no longer needed

indicators.note: to scrap something is to break it up, so the letters of the following words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Throw away a worthless old sixpence since it is now surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was a British sixpence coin before decimal currency; here 'Scrap' simply rearranges DUD TANNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redundant is superfluous, surplus to requirements, which is what no longer needed describes.

clue.text: Nick beset by vermin, getting germ

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: mice are a familiar kind of household vermin
to nick is British slang for to steal, so it means rob

explanation.surface: A thief surrounded by rodents picks up an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is a microorganism that causes disease, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Wish to throw gentleman in river

indicators.note: in, after throw, says the gentleman is put inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
sir is the polite form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone longing to toss a man into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to throw' joins the definition to the wordplay; the River Dee is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A desire is a longing or want, a straight synonym for a wish.

clue.text: Doctor behind rough outline

parts.note: aft is the nautical word for behind or towards the stern

explanation.surface: A physician at the back sketches a quick plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version of a document or plan, which is a rough outline.

clue.text: Poor speaker must utter erratically to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone bad at public speaking is bound to talk unevenly at times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratically' looks like an anagram signal but the answer lies in plain sight across muST UTTERERratically.
explanation.definitionFit: A stutterer repeats sounds involuntarily when talking, so is a person with faltering speech.

clue.text: Almost part with sweetheart — it offers a bigger prize

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: a role is an actor's part in a play
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Nearly breaking up with a partner, with jackpot talk on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: In a lottery, an unwon jackpot is carried forward and added to the next draw's prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery jackpot carried over to the next draw swells its top payout, hence the description.

clue.text: Thanks poet for herald's costume

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: Thanking a poet for a ceremonial outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a short tunic bearing a coat of arms, the traditional garment worn by heralds.

clue.text: Military display also includes advanced bike races

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds the others within it

parts.note: too means also
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle racing on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A parade of troops also featuring motorbike racing.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are annual motorcycle road races on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an evening military display of music and marching, as at Edinburgh.

clue.text: Traveller on wheels, hog, streaked madly around

indicators.note: around says one piece is wrapped about the other
madly says the letters of the word before it are wildly jumbled

parts.note: a boar is a male hog

explanation.surface: A pig shooting about on a skating board, leaving streaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges the letters of 'streaked' to SKATEDER, and 'around' says those letters go round the hog; the comma makes the hog look like the traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone riding a board on four small wheels travels on wheels.

clue.text: Ancient Asian city, a spot in desert

indicators.note: in says the first pieces are placed inside the desert word

parts.note: sand is what a desert is made of, standing for it
a mark is a spot or stain

explanation.surface: A small dot on a map of a desert marks an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand, in present-day Uzbekistan, is one of the oldest cities of Central Asia on the Silk Road.

clue.text: Like Big Brother, nail lower masses

indicators.note: masses as a verb means gathers in a heap, so the letters are thrown together afresh

explanation.surface: An instruction to fasten down the common people, totalitarian style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masses' looks like the downtrodden people of the surface but signals rearranging NAIL LOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is the all-seeing dictator in George Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four, so things like him bear the author's name.

clue.text: One's used to press that'll get even and club together

parts.note: flat means even or level
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: An implement that smooths and levels things, combined with a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron is an old heated iron for pressing clothes, so it is a tool used to press.

clue.text: Feel warmth or get tanned — it's a scorcher

indicators.note: to get tanned is to be beaten, so the letters of the words before are knocked about

explanation.surface: Sunbathing advice on a hot day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get tanned' looks like sunbathing but means get beaten, rearranging FEEL WARMTH OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon that projects burning fuel literally scorches its targets.

clue.text: After Bible study, habit is to make amends

indicators.note: after says the habit piece comes following the Bible study piece

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject studying the Bible
a habit is a garment, as worn by monks or nuns, so dress

explanation.surface: Having studied scripture, a monk's customary practice is to atone.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to set it right or compensate for it, which is to make amends.

clue.text: Part of Jacques Tati comedy is not moving

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film by the French comedian is slow and nothing happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'is not moving' as a description: something that stays still is stationary.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless, unchanging in position, which fits a thing that stays put.

clue.text: Hunger sends king into bar

indicators.note: into says the king is placed inside the bar

parts.note: a stave is a wooden bar or rod
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch hits the pub and leaves everyone hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'bar' wants to be a pub but is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer from severe lack of food, to go hungry, so hunger as a verb.

clue.text: Bush is important person in church

definitions.meaning: a bush or shrub bearing elderflowers and elderberries
a senior official in Presbyterian and other churches

explanation.surface: A shrub that ranks highly among the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder is a shrub with white flowers and dark berries, and also a senior lay officer in some churches.

clue.text: Representative of Indian political scandal being talked of?

indicators.note: being talked of says the clue words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: an imagined scandal in Delhi, named with the -gate suffix after Watergate

explanation.surface: A news story about corruption in Indian government.
explanation.walkthrough: Political scandals get the suffix -gate after Watergate; a Delhi one would be Delhigate.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is someone sent to act on behalf of others, so a representative.

clue.text: Film star Richard embracing new style

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Richard Gere is the American actor

explanation.surface: An actor hugging a newcomer in a fashionable way.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind of artistic work, a particular style.

clue.text: Material making newspaper close down

parts.note: an organ is a periodical that speaks for a group, such as a newspaper
to die is to stop working or shut down

explanation.surface: A newspaper folding over the production of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, transparent cotton fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: Inbred local put away

parts.note: a local is British slang for a nearby pub, so an inn
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A pub where interrelated villagers stow things.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' means the nearest pub; 'Inbred' means natural, inborn here, not genetic mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: An innate quality is one present from birth, so it is inbred in the sense of inborn.

clue.text: Poles getting independence — Communist turns more spiteful

parts.note: S and N stand for the south and north poles
I is a common abbreviation for independence or independent

indicators.note: turns says the word for Communist is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a common nickname for a Communist

explanation.surface: Polish people gaining freedom as a Communist becomes nastier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people but means the compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Snider is the comparative of snide, which means sneeringly malicious, so more spiteful.

clue.text: Condemn one to be removed from consciousness

indicators.note: to be removed from means one piece is taken out of the other

parts.note: sentience is the capacity to feel, consciousness
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A judge sentencing someone to lose awareness.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentence a convict is to declare a punishment, which is to condemn.
